name: Siege of El Fasher

sides.name: Sudanese Armed Forces and allied Joint Forces
sides.commander: Abdel Fattah al-Burhan (overall), Joint Forces commanders (former Darfuri rebel groups now allied to the SAF)
sides.strength: The 6th Infantry Division of the SAF, augmented by the Joint Forces (Justice and Equality Movement, Sudan Liberation Army factions) defending the city
sides.casualties: Thousands killed and wounded; civilian death toll in the high thousands

sides.name: Rapid Support Forces
sides.commander: Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti), Abdul Rahim Dagalo (field command in Darfur)
sides.strength: Roughly 20,000 to 30,000 RSF fighters and allied Arab tribal militias besieging the city in successive offensives
sides.casualties: Heavy, unpublished; multiple senior commanders killed

summary: El Fasher is the last major city in Darfur outside Rapid Support Forces control. The RSF began the siege in April 2024 after consolidating the rest of Darfur. The Joint Forces, former Darfuri rebel groups now allied with the army that once fought them, hold the inner city alongside the army's 6th Infantry Division. Famine conditions inside the perimeter were declared by the IPC in August 2024. Successive RSF ground assaults through 2024 and 2025 have not taken the city.
significance: El Fasher is the focal point of what the United Nations has called the worst humanitarian crisis in the world. The siege has produced atrocities against the non-Arab Masalit and Zaghawa communities reminiscent of the early-2000s Darfur genocide, conducted by the same Janjaweed lineage that the RSF descends from. The fall of El Fasher would clear the way for an RSF state within Sudan and complete the partition of the country.
